key_points.point: Laryngeal cancer is a prevalent and aggressive type of head and neck malignancy characterized by high incidence, significant mortality rates, and poor prognosis, particularly in late-stage disease.

Laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma is typically unrelated to human papilloma virus infection and presents substantial challenges in clinical management due to obstructive symptoms and worse overall survival in advanced stages.

Significant molecular alterations including TP53, CDKN2A, PIK3CA, and NOTCH1 mutations have been identified as important participants in laryngeal cancer development, though prognostic biomarkers and mechanisms of progression remain poorly understood.
Immune-related genes and the tumor immune microenvironment have been identified as important prognostic factors in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma, particularly in smoking patients.

Epigenetic modifications, including N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA methylation and histone lactylation, play crucial roles in laryngeal cancer development and progression through regulation of gene expression and cellular processes.

Non-coding RNAs, including circular RNAs, have emerged as important regulators of gene expression in laryngeal cancer with potential applications as diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic biomarkers.
